items.text: Today we have an important update as we have lots of enhancements for the AI, as we know it has been a big topic for the community 😊
Please give it a try and share your feedback regarding the change!

notes.title: Improved AI with the following changes

items.text: Based on the mods: Rising Tide - Adaptive AI (Huge shout-out to Val for their amazing work!).
The AI scales now based on the Tidefall you are in.
The AI gains economic bonuses in every technological era. This results in a fairer early game, with a rival still standing at the end, and now includes Food and Approval
In Adept, Hero, Stellar, and Endless modes, the AI builds units and districts more cheaply
The AI army bonuses (Unit health, damage, and veterancy) scale with Tidefalls survived
Upkeep decreases with each Tidefall, so the AI will no longer bankrupt itself the moment it loses a territory
Additional comment: we reduced the initial bonuses the AI received based on difficulty to compensate that we were adding this layer.

notes.title: Have AI personality play a larger role in decision-making

items.text: Currently, the AI focuses heavily on building a military if threats have a stronger military than it does. It's an all-or-nothing strategy, so we want different personalities to approach it differently
The Necrophage and Order of Zelevas try to out-military you
The Tahuks and Last Lords take a riskier strategy, continuing to invest in the economy for long-term gains
Have the AI "spread out" on the map and seek regions away from other players:
Currently, the Necrophage especially loves to start right next to other players' starting regions, regardless of the difficulty setting
We changed this so the AI in Sandbox, Easy, and Normal modes will try to spread out, regardless of their faction traits
However, AI in Serious, Impossible, and Endless modes will tend to close in and put pressure on the player

notes.title: Be more peaceful on lower difficulty levels

items.text: Currently, the AI won't declare war on you early on the easiest difficulty levels, but it will still attack your armies, sack your camps, etc
We want to extend that to any aggressive action, giving players on the easiest difficulty levels a buffer
Corrected District level 1, Villages and Extractors not giving the right score
Lowered the score given by foundations and increase the score given by districts lvl 1, 2 and 3 so that the city development score is more accurate
Increased the score given by technologies
Lowered the score given by protectorate and treaties, as it was inflating the Aspects' score
Lowered the score given by population and population types, as 1 unit of population was giving more points than its actual impact

[p align="start"]We've added a little more flavor to major and minor factions, improved some victory objectives, stopped the AI from sniping you while you're still reading a notification, and gave the Necrophage a bit of a safety net, among many other improvements and bugfixes.
[p align="start"]You can read more about these improvements below, and find the full patch notes at the end of the blog.
[p align="start"]In this update we focused on adding a little more flavor to major and minor factions, while also fixing numerous bugs.

[p align="start"]One of the strong points of the Endless games is the asymmetry between factions in both gameplay and lore. Each of them offers their own distinct perspective on the Endless Universe. However, in Endless Legend 2 this perspective was only reflected in the main faction quest and the custom lines in other quests. When it came to the awakening of Saiadha, perhaps the most important event of their lifetimes, every faction encountered the same characters, had the same interactions and reactions. Until now.

[p align="start"]With the Summer Solstice update, we're introducing distinct Awakening Quests for each major factions, giving you a better look into how they react to this cataclysmic upheaval. You can see an example below, if you don't mind spoilers.

[p align="start"]The major factions are not the only ones to get more flavor in this update. While the minor factions already had their own pacification quests and flavor through their units and assimilation bonuses, they all felt very similar when you first encountered them. They all started spawning roaming armies at the same time and the same pace, their armies were all the same size. Apart from the peaceful/hostile distinction, they behaved very similarly on the map. With this update, we're introducing more variety to that. Different minor factions will spawn armies sooner or later, more or less frequently, field larger or smaller armies, or even provide special bonuses when defeating them. Some examples below:
Ochlings spawn new armies frequently, and they can have more armies than other minor factions, swarming your territory if you do not deal with them.
Blackhammers have bigger garrisons in their villages
Consortium armies provide greater battle spoils as you steal salvage their trade goods.

[p align="start"]The old Victory objective to "Pacify X villages" has been changed to control X Pacified Villages. This prevents a problem where it could become impossible to win via this victory because there aren't enough un-pacified villages left to reach the objective. But it also means that now you can always take territories to pursue this victory, or take territories from your opponents to keep them from winning.

[p align="start"]There is a separate victory condition about the total amount of territories claimed, but we like that for this one specific territories (especially those with 3 villages) matter more and will cause you to consider the map differently as you attempt to conquer Saiadha.

[p align="start"]Since the beginning of Amplitude with Endless Space, our games have always used simultaneous turns to keep you playing rather than waiting for the AI to finish their turns. However, it can be frustrating when the AI attacks you while you are busy dealing with something else, especially if you are a new player and don't expect it. So with this Update we are introducing a change to the turn structure: The AI will now not move any of its armies until after you click the "end turn" button. They will still do their economic and diplomatic actions, though, to keep the time waiting for them to take their turn as short as possible.
[p align="start"]For those of you who prefer the old simultaneous turns, you can re-enable them in the game settings in the New Game lobby.

[p align="start"]As an aggressive, ever-warring faction, the Necrophage can be quite difficult to tackle. Their success is built on the momentum of their victories and conquests, so big losses might leave you struggling to find your footing, especially early on. We've been reading your feedback and we're introducing a few changes that should help you recover from setbacks and losses. Broadly speaking:

More Passive Sources of Corpses: Some effects that generated Corpses for you every turn have been expanded to affect all admin centers or farms, not just your capital. [p align="start"]We’ve rebuilt the quest interface to make storytelling smoother, richer, and more engaging.

[p align="start"]​At the beginning of the Early Access, the community shared their disappointment about how the narrative presentation from ENDLESS Legend 1 was missing, and that the experience felt “too click-heavy”. This is something we couldn't change quickly, and we have been working in the “shadows” for months to improve this crucial part.

[p align="start"]Now, quests will be fully displayed with an initial text to setup the scene, along with nice art. Dialogue between characters now plays automatically, reducing the need to click through multiple “next” prompts.

[p align="start"]​After the recent changes we made to the faction, we couldn’t miss the opportunity to rework their main quest a bit, to better highlight their identity and faction archetype, as well as incorporate the different feedback we received from the community.
[p align="start"]Here are some words from Nitya, Senior Narrative Game Designer, to explain the intention of the changes
We've tried to align the design of the quest with the Faction rework

The first chapter was heavily focused on exploration with the missing Pryjza and Necro fight. We've basically swapped the first and second chapters to make sure we start with a "builder"/turtle archetypal chapter, which is then followed by some exploration objectives.

We've also experimented with adding choices very early on: We've tried something completely new of having choices within choices. This creates 4 branches within chapter 1. Since the first chapters are often replayed, this should offer more replayability very early on, which felt crucial.
Pryjza was going missing A LOT, so chapter 3 is now more of an investigation and less of (another) rescue mission.
We centered the narrative on being a breakaway faction for the UE: being estranged, outnumbered on a foreign planet
Since they are so few, it explains why Pryjza's disappearance was worth investigating: every soldier matters to face threats
The ties with UE were also made clearer, and references should also be more obvious.
Some branches were cut (all of the different ways to track Brezvez whereabouts, for instance, picking up curiosities around locations) to make sure the objectives are always compelling.
[p align="start"]​In a similar way to the Kin of Sheredyn, we received plenty of feedback regarding the narration and the tone used by the Necrophage. We’ve been working hard to address this.
[p align="start"]Letting Nitya, Senior Narrative Game Designer, share the main changes

notes.title: The main rework was about the tone of the quest

items.text: Necrophage had to feel dangerous and not just strong.
They were lacking this "awe-inspiring aspect": they are not rational beings but driven by instinct, and that needed to appear more
The dialogues also aim at conveying the feeling that they are a hive, a living organism, with the sum of all their individual making the whole greater than its parts

The rework also aims at better explaining why the outsiders are seen as an opportunity to know more about this world and present ambivalent feelings of the hive: Not every necrophage favors them being kept prisoners. Some wish to feed on them.
It was also an opportunity to incorporate gameplay mechanics in the narration (for instance, talking about the infection into larvae mechanics)
We have also reduced branches that did not trigger very often:
There are now fewer branches but more compelling objectives (for instance, removing the branch asking to ransack a hero haven)
Reducing the number of branches allows us to make sure every objective presented is interesting gameplay-wise

[p align="start"]While balancing costs/yields is always an ongoing topic, we noticed that there were some issues with how district cost were scaling, which was generating frustration among players
[p align="start"]> Thanks to everyone who shared feedback on this topic 🤗

[p align="start"]The issue was, mainly, that the cost was skyrocketing as there was exponential factor in the formula. The base was not bad, as we want players to have choices that are impactful, but this ended up having the opposite effect.

[p align="start"]We released an initial hotfix for this issue that made some districts cheaper, to check with the community if the direction we wanted to go in was right. There was positive feedback, and we decided to keep pushing the idea! Here is how works now 👇
[p align="start"]We made a clearer distinction between the 2 types of districts; Basic & Elite
Elite: Laboratories, Merchant House, Forums & Keeps
[p align="start"]The idea is that the cost of a district will increase mainly if you build the same district, and the rest of the districts will have almost no impact on it.

[p align="start"]Now, the basic costs are way lower (compared to the elite ones), and the idea behind is that you should now be able to build plenty of them, as they are the “foundations” of your city.
[p align="start"]Here is an example of how the formula has evolved for Basic and Elite districts.
10000 min (149 + Target.DistrictCountMoney * 149 + (1 + Target.DistrictCountAnyDistricts / 1.2) ^ 3), but at most 10000
[p align="start"]Let me share an example so you can see the cost (in turns) in a medium city
[p align="start"]As we just talked about districts, we decided to enhance some of them to create a “puzzle system“ that will generate additional synergies between them
[p align="start"]After some feedback from players who tried the PTB, we added additional synergies for the Trading Post and Bridges. And also adjusted some values related to Approval.
[p align="start"]In order to more precisely control how much influence and dust a player can generate, we decided to make 2 major changes to vocations:
Scribes now focus purely on Science (no more Influence)
Citizens and Artisans give slightly less Dust, bringing them in line with the other changes
[p align="start"]This change will also make some of the minor faction populations more interesting! ​

[p align="start"]Now, when a player attacks an enemy unit for the first time, the enemy performs a counter‑attack that deals 70% of its base damage. We think it will improve combat even further. Here are the main goals from the Game Designers behind the change
The first goal is to create attrition in fights and limit alpha strike potential
The second goal is to add one more factor to consider when making decisions in battle, while also creating opportunities for content and stronger unit personality (f*** those pesky Ochlings).
[p align="start"]As this means your units will get more damage, we increased the HP of all units, and also adjusted some skills and added new ones 👀

[p align="start"]Thanks to everyone who shared feedback during the Public Test Branch > we have reduced the defense values (as there were too high) and made additional changes to some units based on your feedback!
[p align="start"]😎 A personal favorite > We added a skill for Defender Heroes that will disable retaliation to all adjacent enemies.
[p align="start"]The team created a new Militia Panel, so you have a better understanding of what Militia you have in your city, as well as in the territories attached to it.

[p align="start"]Sharing a bit of context: in a previous update, we changed the militia to be territory-based instead of having a central one. This was a great change, but it was a bit obscure for players to find out what their militia composition was (it was hidden in a tooltip inside another tooltip).
[p align="start"]Also, everyone can access this information, so be careful, as the AI will be more inclined to attack areas you have left unprotected! 👀
[p align="start"]💡 Do not forget that if you mouse over the flag in the city, you can see how much fortification is required in order to upgrade the militia.
[p align="start"]💡 There are techs that increase the veterancy of your militia
[p align="start"]So happy to share to the entire community that the game now is Steam Deck Verified 🎉

[p align="start"]While we are targeting the next big update to have all the changes to the scaling cost, we want to drop a first patch.

[p align="start"]For this update, we reduced the scale cost of what we will call "basic district".
[p align="start"]The idea is that those buildings are more common to build, and therefore it should be cheaper / not scaling thaaat much.
[p align="start"]Basic District = Farm, Works, and Communal Habitation
[p align="start"]Here is the formula, for those of you interested in it (example below)
👨‍🏫 Cost base 60 plus 30 for every Farm/Works you already have, +10 for every district you already have (except the city center)
Note: To avoid overflow, the cost in Industry will cap at 5,000. Remove the city center from consideration by subtracting 1.
👨‍🏫 Cost base 60 plus 15 for every Communal Habitatation you already have, +5 for every district you already have (except the city center)
Example 1 > You are building ONLY Farms
Example 2 > You are building other buildings than Farms
Number of Any other Districts than Farm
Both situations are different, as the formula takes into consideration the number of X districts you already built and the total number of districts.
[p align="start"]Also, we incorporated a max cost to avoid scaling "To Infinite and Beyond."

​Our Lead Game Designer recently released a blog with more information on the rationale behind the changes, so allow me here to quote him;
Let's be honest: diplomacy in its previous form had a bit of a goldfish problem.
Raze an empire's city? They're naturally upset for a while.
Raze it again? Still upset, same amount.
Raze it a third time, burn down their Ministry, occupy half their territory? Still... the same upset.
The world had no sense of escalation, no memory.
You could be the most relentless conqueror in the history of Saiadha and the other empires would essentially treat each act of aggression as if it were the first.
In order to help with this situation, we introduced 2 main changes:
There are certain actions that will stack Public Opinion from other empires.
Each time you perform a hostile (or friendly) action toward an Empire, a counter climbs.
Badges are the centerpiece of this update. They represent a pattern of behavior so consistent that it defines how the other empire sees you.

This helps the AI remember what your behavior has been like towards them in the early game, so no more “we are super friends after you destroyed half of their empire”. This is not an impediment to having diplomacy with them, but it will be a bit harder, as players will be accountable for their behavior.
Here is an example of how it works
5+ attacks → Attacked III (-30, 15 turns) → Bully badge (-20, permanent)
If you want to de-escalate the situation, you must go one level at a time. Let’s assume you are currently in “Attack II”, you will need to wait 15 turns in order to go to Attacked I.

Improved how AI perceives threats in the world

It's a subtle change... Basically, to decide which army can perform which military mission where, the AIs maintain a metric that states how dangerous each region is. To compute this metric, it looks at all the foreign armies in each region, assesses the threat it represent, and gets a magic number. The threat generated by each army can be propagated from one region to another. So far, this propagation was a bit simple (as in "the threat can propagate through x regions"). The issue with this approach is that the regions we consider are not equally sized. Some are as large as a territory, others as small as a borough... My goal here is to account for these different sizes when computing the propagation.
So it does affect the way the AI looks at all the other armies, so its decision-making should be generally a bit better, but it won't make a night-and-day difference

items.text: [p align="start"]After some weeks of PTB, we are now ready to release the next update, Echoes of Creation!
[p align="start"]Thanks to everyone who has participated and shared feedback or reported issues 🌟
[p align="start"]Here, the goal is clear, letting the imagination of players go wild and allowing them to create interesting/Overpower/Absurd/crazy factions.
[p align="start"]Here is an example of a nice Necrophage that will spread Coral and perhaps heal their units like Last Lords 🎃
[p align="start"]If you are interested in knowing more, do not hesitate to check the fun blog made by Nitya, one of our game designers 👇

[p align="start"]🚨 A little disclaimer 🚨 > There are no quests (from the main major faction quests) for Custom Factions! This has some effects, for instance, the Chosen unit is not available (as it is unlocked by completing the quest).
[p align="start"]Also, Custom Factions are not available to be played in Multiplayer. We are working on this!

[p align="start"]What is it? It is a new visual layer you can activate in the bottom-left of the screen, which will indicate with colours + icons the type of buildings in your city. It will help those of you who wanted a clear and quick view of all the buildings you had.
[p align="start"]Above 👆, you can see the icon and colours surrounding the buildings. But if you zoom out for the strategic view, we move to a “simpler view”, mainly showing coloured icons 👇

[p align="start"]Around the end of the game (around the latest 30 turns before finishing the game, on normal speed), the Endless Monsoon will trigger! This will have a direct effect on Saiadha, making the world darker and more dangerous for everyone 😨
[p align="start"]Be careful, as it will unleash the Keeper of the Depths 😨

[p align="start"]In this update, we have improved the AI in several aspects, such as: increasing its desire of expansion into new territories, better fulfilment of victory conditions, finer population allocation, enhancement of the use of defense instance in battle, etc.
[p align="start"]This is an ongoing topic to improve, but since there are quite a few elements, it deserves a bit of attention, so feel free to share your thoughts 💡
[p align="start"]Cannot wait to see the evolution and your feelings afterwards!!

[p align="start"]From the beginning of the early access, we noticed that some players were confused about how victory conditions worked, in the sense that they thought all objectives (on a path) were mandatory, instead of just needing one of them.
[p align="start"]We have done some work on this area and now it should be more intuitive, as all objectives of the path will now be mandatory.
[p align="start"]In this example, in order to win with the Impress path, you will be required to fulfill the science and the minor faction objectives.

[p align="start"]A small reminder that on this screen you can see how the other major empires are progressing on each of the paths. Additionally, this choice will have an impact on the relationship with other empires.
[p align="start"]Let me share the words from the Game Design team, as it is a nice summary of their intentions.
“To exercise greater control over the initial balancing of Science and Influence resources, we have reconfigured certain technologies to unlock the Laboratory, Forum, and Keep districts in Era 2.
To maintain the same number of technologies in each era as before, some district improvements have been moved towards Era 1.
Additionally, certain factions will not undergo these changes in order to maintain their districts in the 1st era (Kin with the Keep, Tahuks with the Laboratory, and Aspects with the Forum).”
[p align="start"]During the PTB, we saw a positive reaction from players to this change. But let us know your thoughts after playing a few games!
[p align="start"]Here you can see the initial districts for the Kin of Sheredyn in Era 1
[p align="start"]And here once you arrive in Era 2.

[p align="start"]In the case of the Kin, they do have access to the Keep district on Era 1, but that is due to asymmetry of the faction. The same will happen to Tahuk and their Laboratories. Otherwise, those 3 buildings will be delayed to Era 2.
[p align="start"]No worries, as you will have additional improvements in era 1 to compensate for this.

notes.title: Heroes Skills + Equipment have been rebalanced

items.text: [p align="start"]Here are the areas that have been tweaked and adjusted.
[p align="start"]These changes are part of the borader balancing work the team started with the last update, which gives more importance to hero attributes.
[p align="start"]Here is a small showcase of the minor faction skill tree, which has changed significantly.

[p align="start"]Some of the skills/elements might feel a bit overpowered. Why? You will notice in the roadmap (more below) that we will introduce combat retaliation, and the balancing we have done is contemplating that (for future update). Otherwise, we would need to rebalance everything again in “a couple of months”. Once this change is introduced, we will also increase the HP of all units, which will result in better overall balance.
[p align="start"]This might look like a small change, but it actually represents a swap in how the system works, and it will impact the defensive/military aspects of the game.
[p align="start"]Previously, there was a common and unified militia for all cities/camps, based on the militia level of the city (which you could improve with techs).
[p align="start"]Now it will be territory-based and will scale depending on the specific fortification level of each city.
"We wanted to create opportunities for attackers by making the attached territories more vulnerable. Making it territory based solve this intention.

The defenders also now depend on the fortification instead of the technologies. Reaching a certain amount of fortification now defines the units defending the city or admin center. The technologies still impact the militia as researching military techs now give veterancy level to defenders.
A combination of technologies, military districts, and infrastructure will be the key to keeping the borders safe.
Attacking vulnerable territories is now an option instead of rushing the city.
I'm waiting for your feedbacks of the feature now that we have a first pass of content that should help you experiment in good conditions a proper siege warfare."

[p align="start"]In the example above, you can see the main capital has 1050 fortification, which means a threshold 3 for militia. And even if you cannot see it here, the attached territory only has 600 fortification, which results in a lower tier militia. Players will need to decide where to allocate resources in order to defend key strategic positions.
[p align="start"]We have also included some techs that will improve the veterancy of your militia!
[p align="start"]You will find all the details in the patchnotes below , as this rework comes with balancing adjustements of infrastructure, districts, and techs (fortification-related).
[p align="start"]There are some smaller changes/new quality-of-life changes that are easy to miss, but we do think they deserve special attention. Some of them have been heavily requested by players:
✨ Updated Luxury resource deposits to appear right from the start
✨ Added filters in the construction menu to filter out improvements already built or locked
✨ Added the possibility to multi-sell equipment
✨ Updated district layer when zoomed out to include district colors
✨ Removed an immersion-breaking side quest on Necrophages
✨ Converted all curiosity events into quests

[p align="start"]We wanted to take this opportunity to update our roadmap to showcase what the team has improved in previous updates, and also to give a hint about some of the elements that will arrive in the next updates!

In case you missed it, here is our latest big update for the game, The Gathering
[p align="start"]We are about to leave for Christmas, and we wanted to drop a major update for the game 🎅
[p align="start"]Let's present The Gathering, which brings lots of big changes, and most importantly, multiplayer!

[p align="start"]Players have been experiencing some confusion about how you build districts in the game, and found it counter-intuitive. Due to this, we have decided to make it closer to our previous titles!
Now, you will choose the type of district you want to build, you will get a "best location suggestion" (with FIDSI outcome), and then you will decide the tile where it will be placed.
This also takes into consideration if the location will level up other districts (like the image below)
[p align="start"]To tell you more about the reasons and the intentions behind it, you can check this blog from Pierre, a game designer.
Hey bosses, we made some changes to the Necrophages: we are experimenting with faction asymmetry, and the first victim of this experimentation is the bugs.
This update is more about the Economy part rather than the military aspect of the loved(n't) bugs.

[p align="start"][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3407390/view/498339977282717103?l=english"]There have been changes in how the districts evolve (different from other factions), and "instant building" for special Necrophage districts that costs only corpses (so players need to decide if they keep upgrading units or focus on the economy), and more...
[p align="start"]You no longer need to go the the beta branch in order to play multiplayer!
[p align="start"]Everyone can access it directly from the main menu!
[p align="start"]Please, if you encounter any issues, share them with us! This will help us to identify and solve issues (like desyncs) 🙏
[p align="start"]Here is our first big step to improving narration 💪

[p align="start"]We improved the flow to make it less "clicky" (just pressing Next 8 times) but closer to how it is on EL1. Now we will have an initial paragraph that works as a setup of the situation, followed by two or three lines of dialogue based on your faction, and then it goes straight to the objective.
[p align="start"]What do you think about this change?

[p align="start"]We are making some changes in diplomacy to make it more engaging and dynamic. Signing a treaty on turn 10 and forgetting about the topic was not "very fun"... Therefore, you will have certain treaties that will last only 30 turns.

[p align="start"]Also, you will be able to compliment and insult the other factions. This gives players more direct ways to influence factions' opinions (it was difficult to get into "justified wars").
[p align="start"]Something that has frequently been asked for by a part of the community and here it is! Also, we adapted the normal game speed turn limit to make it more fitting for our vision
[p align="start"]As a reminder, you can still keep playing "one more turn" after reaching the turn limit, but it's "at your own risk".
[p align="start"]Quite a few changes to Aspects to make them "even more Aspects" hahah.
Regarding these changes, I give the mic to Nicolas 👇
Today, we're excited to share a deep dive into the latest improvements for the Aspects, our diplomacy-oriented faction.
These changes reinforce their identity as a people who thrive through cooperation, symbiosis, and shared growth rather than domination.
Let’s take a look at how their playstyle evolves, and how these new mechanics bring their harmony-through-coral philosophy to life.

The Aspects have always stood apart: part-machine, part-coral, and wholly interdependent with the planet. But their gameplay needed stronger tools to express that identity. Before diving into the changes, here is a quick reminder of their defining pillars:
The Aspects lean into soft power: influence, negotiation, and cooperative economic ties with anyone willing to listen… or simply stand near the coral.
2. A True Symbiosis Between Robot and Coral
Their coral structures shouldn’t just spread — they should feed, support, and shape the world.

Coral is no longer a purely Aspects-only advantage. Other players benefit from its spread — a mechanic that invites collaboration, tension, or opportunism, depending on how one approaches the Aspects’ “gifts.”
[p align="start"]With these foundations, let’s explore their latest evolution 🧬
Coral bonuses used to be subtle — sometimes too subtle.

notes.title: To make the ecosystem feel alive and valuable for everyone

items.text: → Every Coral tile now grants +1 Food.
Provides tangible early-game value to coral spread across the world.
The Aspects now gain an additional unlock in a Era II technology:
This is a crucial tool for an influence-focused faction.
Now Influence becomes a flexible resource for military, economy, or political development — reflecting their mastery of soft power.
The Aspects are a population-heavy faction, but previously lacked tools to offset the Approval penalties that growth created.
A simple, powerful stabilizer for growing cities — and a thematic reinforcement of their caretaker nature.
Coral expansion remains essential, but its pace was snowballing too quickly:
→ Coral now spreads naturally every 7 turns
This slows runaway map coverage and makes coral-spore placement more deliberate.
But to offset this slower pace, coral spread gains new advantages…

notes.title: Coral-Touched Minor Factions village Gain New Rules

items.text: Minor Factions play an important role in Aspects’ identity — especially as part of their shared symbiosis. We’ve added two major changes:
1. Coralized Villages Now Spread Coral to Adjacent Tiles
Villages naturally amplify the coral ecosystem, reinforcing the idea that the coral “grows toward life.”
2. Village touched by Coral now have Bribe Cost: –100%
More agency in pacifying minors when using your armies,
Insurance that automatic coral pacification no longer disrupts pacification quests,
A reliable way for the Aspects to remain competitive militarily by rallying stronger Minor Factions.
→ Laboratories, Farms & Works now have double adjacency bonuses

The Aspects thrive when interconnected with nature so the three districts playing with natural feature now reflect that. This dramatically enhances city planning potential and rewards thoughtful layouts.
The Aspects renounce the Dust District entirely.
→ Removes access to the Dust District
This fully expresses their non-Dust, symbiosis-based identity.
The latest changes strengthen the Aspects in every dimension of their core fantasy:
A living, useful coral ecosystem, now feeding the world and shaping tile strategy.
Smoother population growth and stability thanks to Guardians.
Deeper interactions with Minor Factions, enabling both pacification and military relevance.
Enhanced city-building depth through double adjacency bonuses.
A clear non-Dust identity, fully embracing organic synergy over Dust production.

notes.title: 🌟 Here are the main highlights of this update 🌟

items.text: We have improved the specialization path, so they feel a bit more different. Due to this we have decided to make adjustment to all units (stats, skill, etc.)
You can check the BLOG FROM PIER that explain a bit more on the logic behind the changes.
Thanks to all player that participated on the Public Test Branch (PTB) as we have done some additional adjustment based on your feedback.
Units start losing defense when multiple enemy units are adjacent to them (Starting with 3 adjacent enemy units). This debuff will go progressively from 3 enemies (-25% defense) to 6 (-100% defense).
If you unit does not have an armor, do not worry, there won´t be any penalty
🏰 Cities no longer blocking tiles in battle
We heard your feedback that cities were causing battles to have a smaller area to fight. We totally agree that caused some frustrations and decided to remove cities completely from the battleground.

We received feedback that Doomwraiths were too impactful They are tough units, and their corruption effect was crippling cities, making it difficult to produce units to counter them. Corruption applied by Doomwraiths to cities is now less severe and now increase over time, reaching up to 50% after 10 turns.
We know that for some players are still an easy target, but we are having additional improvements for them in the future, no worries!
The team has improved how is the general display of the tech screen and make the techs that have been researched more distinguished (compared to the "non-researched")
Similar on how it will be in multiplayers (it is the case as well for our previous game), we added an option on the UI Settings that will display always the turn status for the AI and the World.
This will help to those player that prefer to wait a few seconds prior starting doings some action.

We noticed that some players were experiencing crashes that were caused by the automated sync that we use for storage the save files (Documents > Endless Legend 2). This was the case by some providers, such us OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, etc.
Do not worry, you do not need to do/change anything we automatically move everything to
If you experienced any trouble, please let us know!

Literally 35 pages on a Word document 😱

Rebalanced the experience required for heroes to level up. Heroes now require less experience to reach level 5, and more experience beyond level 5.
Non-hero units now require significantly more experience to gain veterancy levels.
Veterancy now grants +10% Health, +10% Damage, and +3 Defense (previously +5% Health, +5% Damage, and +2 Defense).
The values of the "Military Discipline I" and "Military Discipline II" Era Unlocks have been updated to reflect the changes in the experience formula.
The values of the "Expert Instruction I", "Expert Instruction II" and "Expert Instruction III" Era Unlocks have updated to reflect the changes in the experience formula.

We have also rebalanced most units — you can find the details at the end!

When more than two units are adjacent to an enemy unit, that unit suffers a significant Defense penalty.
If the unit does not have any defense, it won't suffer any penalty

Today we end our first week after releasing in Early Access and we couldn't be happier 😁
Thanks to all of you that who have tried the game and have been sharing feedback and bugs with us! This has helped the team a lot in order to fix the most urgent matters ✨

As you can imagine 5 days 5 updates is REAAAALLYY good, but it is not something that can be sustain for perpetuity. Now, we need to focus on a bigger update that cover more things than just hotfixes (like military adjustments, balancing, etc.).
We will be sharing more information of what is coming next really soon 🔥

items.text: Thank your for sharing all your feedback and reviews of the game! We couldn't be here without all your support ✨

Hey everyone, another day, another update! Apart from hotfixes we wanted to do a quick balancing pass to most of the victory conditions as we know it has been a point of discussion among the community.
